To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
disruption of the mouse dyenine heavy chain 7 gene (DNAH7, HDHC7) leads to asthenozoospermy and reduced ciliary beating frequency.
mice lacking the dynein heavy-chain gene MDHC7 are viable but male MDHC7(-) mice are infertile due to the absence of inner dynein arms and a reduced ciliary beat.
disruption of the mouse dyenein heavy chain gene MDHC7 results in asthenospermia, and reduced ciliary beating frequency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new gene involved in the etiology of PCD.
the function of the inner dyenein arm and its role in ciliary and flagellum motility.
the function of the dynein heavy chains in the inner dyneins of the flagella and cilia and the importance of these proteins for the generation of the ciliary and flagella beat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the loss of the MDHC7 gene results in astheno- and oligozoospermia, and in a reduced tracheal ciliary beat frequency, which are the hallmarks of primary ciliary dysgenesis.
MDHC7 is a novel gene essential for the motility of spermatozoa and tracheal ciliated cells.
MDHC7(-/+) and MDHC7(+/+) mice have normal sperm tail and cilia function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have generated a mouse model for the human ciliary dyskineisa syndrome.

we have generated the first mouse model of PCD caused by a mutation in an inner dynein heavy-chain gene, and that this mouse model will be very useful for further studies on the function of dynein heavy chains and on PCD.
the MDHC7 gene is a candidate for PCD in humans and mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the loss of MDHC7 function results in a severe asthenozoospermy, and that the loss of this dynein isoform in humans may result in a form of PCD.
the MDHC7 gene is a good candidate gene to explain PCD in humans and that the mouse model is a good model system to investigate the molecular basis of this disease.
MDHC7(-/+) and MDHC7(+/+) mice are normal and that MDHC7 deficiency is not a major cause of infertility.
